_provenance.what: Every unit of time from the paramāṇu to Brahmā's life: the ratio the engine computes with, every attestation a local text gives (with its file and line or verse), the loci the code claims, the owner's attributions, the other ladders in the owner's repositories, and the conflicts between them. Built 2026-10-08 from the verified research of that day (the owner: 'add the Purāṇas and Upaniṣads from which the time ladder and names were built').
_provenance.decisions: Owner, 2026-10-08. P1: the engine's chain stays canonical (canonical, below); the other ladders are alternative readings (ladders). 'pala' = 1/60 ghaṭī = vināḍī everywhere; vipala = 1/60 pala [standard; no local text]. P2: the Bhagavad Gītā, the Chāndogya Upaniṣad, the Navagraha Stotra, the Bhāgavata and the Viṣṇu Purāṇa are in no repository; the owner's attributions to them are recorded as class owner-statement, status 'awaiting edition' (corpus/parampara/registry.json), with a locus only where a repository file gives one, and are upgraded to [text] when an edition is added. No verse and no verse number is supplied before then.
_provenance.quotes: Every 'from' is a local file and line (editions/…html:N), a BPHS verse (corpus/bphs/canon.json#chapter.verse), or a line of an e-text kept outside the repository (etext:<file>:N), whose quoted lines are copied in corpus/parampara/etext-lines.json. 'sa' is verbatim from that line. A reference in another of the owner's repositories is given as 'at' (not checked here) and is never [text]. This repository's code is cited by its symbol, 'symbol': '<file> <NAME>' (e.g. math-core.js SUBDAY_CHAIN), never by a line number, so a citation does not move when the file grows; parampara.test.js checks that the file declares the name and that SUBDAY_CHAIN is the chain below.
_provenance.derive: Each attestation that states a ratio carries 'states' (1 unit = equals × of) and 'expr', an expression over numberWords whose inflected 'forms' stand in the quoted lines; parampara.test.js evaluates it and checks it gives 'equals'. Expressions: a stem; {"×": [...]} product; {"+": [...]} sum; {"bh": [...]} bhūtasaṅkhyā, first word the units.
_provenance.tags: [text] stated by a local source edition or e-text; [reading] this repository's reading of it; [standard] a convention of the tradition no local text states; [claim-only] stated in code or derived prose with no local source; [owner-statement] the owner's attribution, no local edition; [theorem] exact arithmetic on the stated numbers.

spandaFactor.note: the 13th factor, 100 spandas to a paramāṇu, has no located source; its arithmetic role is to make 1″ of the turn a whole number of cells (3,280,500,000 ÷ 1,296,000 = 10125/4 paramāṇu, so ×4 would already do); the name 'spanda' is shared with the Spanda-kārikā, which states no unit or ratio

canonical.ahoratra: kala-dvara.js counts the lattice per turn of the star-wheel (SS 1.12's nākṣatra ahorātra; SS 13.23's bowl sinks sixty times in it); math-core.js counts it per civil day. Both are 'the ahorātra' of the chain; the caller says which (kala-dvara.js SPANDAS_PER_DAY).
canonical.agreesWithText: 60 nāḍikā to the ahorātra = SS 1.12's 60 nāḍī; one prāṇa of SS 1.11 = 151,875 paramāṇu = 15,187,500 spandas, a whole number. Below the prāṇa the local SS names only the truṭi (1.11) and gives no ratio, so nothing in a local text checks the chain there.

conflicts.what: 'pala' names two sizes 60 times apart: = vināḍī (1/60 ghaṭī) in BPHS 5.8 and 46.90 [reading] and the SS edition's gloss (:220, :373); = 1/60 vināḍī in panchanga.js's sexagesimal {ghati, vinadi, pala} and the design document (VEDHA-YANTRA-DESIGN-2026-10-07.md:65-66, '31 vi 31 pala 24').
conflicts.resolution: decision P1: pala = 1/60 ghaṭī = vināḍī everywhere. panchanga.js's third place should be named vipala (it is 1/60 vināḍī); that file belongs to another stage (listed as outside this stage).

conflicts.what: vipala (1/60 pala = 1/10 prāṇa, 216,000 a day) is named by no local source text; the SS edition's gloss uses it (:220); vedic-ghadi's 'Diti' cascade makes a vipala of 10.8 s.
conflicts.resolution: decision P1: vipala = 1/60 pala [standard; no local text]. On the lattice it is 1,518,750 spandas, the same size as Āryabhaṭa's gurvakṣara (Kālakriyā 2).

conflicts.what: no local text gives the muhūrta: the canonical chain makes it 2 nāḍikā (30 to the ahorātra) [claim-only]; muhurta.js uses fifteen of the day and fifteen of the night as standard usage; BPHS 3.66-3.68 divide day and night into eight parts each, not fifteen.
conflicts.resolution: kept as the chain gives it, tagged [claim-only]; awaiting an edition (the Brahma-Vaivarta and others are cited in code only).

conflicts.what: BPHS 3.66-3.69 divide the day and the night each into eight parts and name one part ardhaprahara, so the prahara is a quarter of the day or night and eight make the ahorātra [reading]; KAAL maha_sphota.py:98-99 has 7.5 muhūrta to a prahara and 8 prahara to the ahorātra, which makes 60 muhūrta a day.
conflicts.resolution: the BPHS reading is recorded; the KAAL table is inconsistent and is not used.

conflicts.what: SS 14.10 begins the seasons with śiśira, each of two rāśis; read with 14.9 ('tataḥ' = from the Makara saṅkrānti) śiśira is Makara–Kumbha [reading]; sphuta's table begins vasanta at Meṣa (citing the Jyotiṣa-vedāṅga, which is not local).
conflicts.resolution: the SS order is the text's; sphuta's is an alternative reading with no local source.

conflicts.what: kalā as a unit of time: sphuta labels 'SS I.15: 30 kāṣṭhā = 1 kalā, 30 kalā = 1 ghaṭikā', but the local SS 1.15 is the caturyuga verse and no SS verse has a time-kalā; the Mahā-grantha has 30 kalā = 1 muhūrta; KAAL has 15 kalā = 1 nāḍikā; the canonical chain has no kalā (kala-dvara.js uses kalā only as the minute of arc, = the prāṇa of the turn).
conflicts.resolution: no time-kalā is used; three disagreeing claims are listed.

conflicts.what: nimeṣa per ahorātra: 202,500 (canonical chain), 324,000 (sphuta), 405,000 (Mahā-grantha; = 16/75 s of the civil day), 486,000 (KAAL maha_sphota); truṭi < nimeṣa by 900× in the chain and 300× in sphuta; no local text gives a nimeṣa ratio (the Kālanirṇaya, JM p.23, only names it).
conflicts.resolution: decision P1: the canonical chain; the rest are alternative readings (ladders).

conflicts.what: the same 328,050,000,000 is per turn of the star-wheel in kala-dvara.js (SS 1.12's nākṣatra ahorātra) and per civil day in math-core.js; vedic-ghadi and the web site divide the civil day.
conflicts.resolution: the text's ghaṭī is of the turn (SS 1.11-1.12; muhurta.js, panchanga.js); the civil sixtieth is given beside it where printed pañcāṅgas use it.

conflicts.what: SS 1.18-1.20: a manvantara of 71 yugas with a Kṛta-length sandhi, a kalpa of 1000 yugas; Āryabhaṭa (Kālakriyā 8): Brahmā's day is 1008 yugas (14 Manus × 72, as Nīlakaṇṭha reads the Gītikā).
conflicts.resolution: two local texts differ; the engine's SS canon takes 1000, the 'aryabhata' canon's yuga integers do not depend on it.

conflicts.what: SS 14.14 makes the lunar month a day of the pitṛs; Āryabhaṭa's Kālakriyā 7 makes the pitṛs' year thirty human years, which makes their day a solar month; Nīlakaṇṭha argues (abh2.md:316) that the lunar month is meant.
conflicts.resolution: both are listed; neither is used in a computation.

conflicts.what: the 360-day year of Brahmā is not in SS 1.21 (a reading); the Mahā-grantha printed Brahmā's year and life 100 times too large (corrected 2026-10-08, editions/maha-grantha-full-edition.html:3784-3787).
conflicts.resolution: 3,110,400,000,000 years a year, 311,040,000,000,000 a life [theorem on the reading].
